about: The advisor findings we accept on purpose (ARCHITECTURE §8.2 rule 4, §11.6). npm run sql:advisors compares get_advisors output (security and performance) with this file: a finding that matches no entry fails, and a required entry with no finding fails. Every entry says why it is accepted. Edit it in the same pull request as the migration that causes the finding.

live.note: After SQL-1's baseline and helpers were applied, the security advisor reported nothing and the performance advisor reported INFO 0005 for exactly the four indexes accepted below. The hosted MCP grouped them as one unused_index lint with four findings, which npm run sql:advisors splits into one lint per finding. A restrictive deny-all policy counts as a policy for lint 0008, so the new tables raise no 0008 finding.

rpc.why: Every RPC is a SECURITY DEFINER function in public that anon is meant to call; that is the whole API (§8.2 rule 2). Lint 0028 flags each one for anon and lint 0029 for authenticated, which keeps EXECUTE because migrations never take a grant away (decisions memo §14.4). Each RPC validates its input, caps payloads and rate-limits itself, so both findings are expected for exactly these names. The list mirrors private.rpc_allowlist: npm run sql:bundle checks that the two agree, and the ticket that adds an RPC adds its name to both. SQL-1 adds none; SQL-2 adds the eleven identity RPCs.

accepted.why: The hourly job prunes counters older than 2 days through this index. Until pg_cron runs it (SQL-8) and the table grows past a few pages, no plan uses it, so INFO 0005 reports it as unused.
The hourly job prunes write keys older than 48 hours through this index; unused until the job runs over a table large enough to scan by index.
delete_player (SQL-2) removes a player's write keys by player id with this index, so the deletion stays an index lookup (AC-DAT-02). Nothing uses it before SQL-2.

§8.3 indexes the error log by time for the owner's triage through MCP (an internal reply shows its reference, and the owner reads the errors logged around it) and for the attended hourly step, which prunes rows older than 30 days. Nothing reads the log before the first RPC that can fail (SQL-2) or before that step runs, so INFO 0005 reports the index as unused.

nightly_players finds test players older than a day through this partial index. Until SQL-8 schedules the nightly job, and the table holds enough test players for a plan to choose it, nothing scans it, so INFO 0005 reports it as unused.

It covers the foreign key to categories (§8.3: every foreign key indexed, lint 0001) and the per-category reads of calibration and pulls (SQL-9). Nothing reads practice items by category before SQL-9, so INFO 0005 reports it as unused.

It covers the foreign key to categories (§8.3, lint 0001), so a category's mysteries are found without a scan. No query reads mysteries by category until the weekly content run's inputs (SQL-9), so INFO 0005 reports it as unused.

It covers the foreign key to answer_entities (§8.3, lint 0001) and finds the mysteries whose answer is an entity, for key corrections and accepted ids (SQL-9). Unused until those run, so INFO 0005 reports it.

It covers the foreign key to categories (§8.3, lint 0001). Nothing reads encores by category in v1, but an unindexed foreign key is lint 0001, which §8.2 accepts only for player_days.attempt_id, so the index stays and INFO 0005 reports it as unused.
It covers the foreign key to categories (§8.3, lint 0001) and serves room hosting by category (SQL-13). Unused until rooms exist, so INFO 0005 reports it.
